items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: But Jimmy had the band, and I joined him... that's when I worked with Chippy Hill and Billy Mitchell... I asked Jimmy if he wanted to make a session with us and he did.

ctx.x: Junie Cobb, right. But Jimmy had the band, and I joined him, and that was when Leon Washington and Gaby Rogers, the piano player, and I don't know who was playing bass at that time, I can't think. But, anyway, that's when I worked with Chippy Hill and Billy Mitchell and all these people,

in this little night -- that's when I was telling you about the night clubs they had. But this was a nice little club, at 23rd and State Street. And I stayed there for about a year or so, and later, Benny Washington replaced me. You remember Benny Washington?

items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I don't mean what is normally called Chicago jazz, like Jimmy McPartland and those guys.

ctx.x: Well, at one time there may -- at one time I think there was. But I think most of the jazz today is just like if you go to New Orleans, you find -- you can find the same kind of jazz you find in Chicago or New York or anywhere. But they stick to their tradition. But Chicago had -- not now --
I don't mean what is normally called Chicago jazz, like Jimmy McPartland and those guys. I don't mean that.
